name: What exterior upgrades are most important before selling a house?

mainEntity.name: Which exterior remodeling projects should I do first before listing a house for sale in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Which exterior remodeling projects should I do first before listing a house for sale in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the goal is to sell, the exterior projects with the highest priority are usually the ones that remove buyer hesitation. That means fixing visible damage, refreshing paint or trim, cleaning hardscape, repairing caulk and sealant, improving the entry, replacing worn lighting, and making landscaping look intentional rather than neglected. In competitive Los Angeles neighborhoods, first impressions matter a lot, so a clean and well-kept façade can do more for resale than a large custom upgrade. Buyers also notice signs of deferred maintenance, such as peeling finishes, warped doors, cracked stucco, stained roofs, or broken gutters. Addressing those issues first makes the home feel cared for and reduces the chance of low offers or inspection concerns. If the budget allows only a few improvements, focus on the front elevation and any visible repairs that photograph poorly. Large-scale luxury features may appeal to some buyers, but the biggest return usually comes from making the exterior look move-in ready and structurally sound.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before selling, the most important exterior upgrades are usually cleanup, paint touch-ups, entry improvements, lighting, basic landscape repair, and fixing visible damage like cracked stucco, rotten trim, or failing caulk. Buyers respond most to a clean, maintained appearance. Major custom work is usually less important than removing obvious signs of neglect.
